Reading the structure region by region:

- **Biphenyl acid part:** The top-left ring carries a CO2H group. It is joined to a second ring, which has an OH ortho to the biaryl bond and an NH-N= hydrazone group on the other side of the OH carbon. That gives a 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl-biphenyl-3'-carboxylic acid.
- **Hydrazone linkage:** The chain is HN–N=C3, where C3 is the isatin 3-position.
- **Isatin core:** C3 is bonded to C2(=O), which is bonded to N1. N1 is fused to the benzo ring, and the benzo ring closes back to C3.
- **N-substituent:** N1 carries a thiophene attached at its 3-position. The adjacent C2 of the thiophene bears the CN group, and the ring sulfur is at the bottom.

Writing the SMILES:

Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccsc3C#N)c3ccccc23)c1O

Thiophene check: c3ccsc3C#N starts at C3 (attached to N), then c (C4), c (C5), s (S1), then c3 (C2) closing the ring back to C3 and carrying the nitrile. This is consistent with the drawing.

Stereochemistry: the C=N bond is drawn with a geometry, but the double bond is at the ring carbon. In the image, the NH is on the upper side of the C=N, pointing toward the C=O side. The N is at the top of the C3=N bond and has NH to its upper left. C3 has the C=O neighbor on its left and the aryl ring on its right. The NH is on the left, so it is syn to the carbonyl, which is the usual Z form. I will leave the stereo out, since the geometry is not clearly marked.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccsc3C#N)c3ccccc23)c1O
